newsitem.title: USA: Houston delays refunding of water revenue bonds.
newsitem.headline: Houston delays refunding of water revenue bonds.

text.p: The City of Houston will test the market again next week to get lower interest rates on a proposed refunding of up to $450 million of water and sewer revenue bonds, a city official said Thursday.

John Baldwin, deputy finance director for the city's public works department, said market conditions were not favorable this week, forcing the department to postpone the refunding of the bonds which currently carry average interest rates of about six percent.

"The refunding will be between $300 million and $450 million. We will test the market next week," he said. "The rates this week were around 5.4 percent, but we would like it lower than that. If we don't succeed next week, we can wait for several more weeks."
He said the department expects the refunding to produce present value savings of between $12 million and $16 million.
The refunding will be done by a team of nine underwriters led by Merrill Lynch & Co. There are three other co-seniors and five co-managers in the team.
The water and sewer department currently has a bonded debt of about $2.5 billion.
